Championship]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2013 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship|2013 Latvia]]|[[Turkey men's national under-18 and under-19 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Cedi Osman''' ({{IPA|tr|ˈdʒedi ˈosman}}; born 8 April 1995) is a Turkish professional [[basketball]] player for [[PAOK BC|PAOK Thessaloniki]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]] (GBL) and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]]. He was drafted with the 31st pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]] and played for the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] and the [[San Antonio Spurs]] over the span of seven seasons. He plays at the [[small forward]] position. ==Early years== Osman was born in [[Ohrid]], Republic of Macedonia (now [[North Macedonia]]) to a [[Turks in North Macedonia|Turkish]] father and a [[Bosniaks of Serbia|Bosniak]] mother (from Novi Pazar, Serbia).{{cite news|title="Zašto ne pričamo na srpskom?!"|url=http://mondo.rs/a828291/Sport/Eurobasket-2015/MONDO-intervju-sa-Dzedijem-Osmanom.html|access-date=7 September 2017|work=mondo.rs|date=9 September 2015|language=sr}}{{cite news|title=Čedi Osman: Duda Ivković? Velika sreća za mene, kakvu u celom životu možda više neću imati|url=http://www.mozzartsport.com/vesti/cedi-osman-duda-ivkovic-velika-sreca-za-mene-kakvu-u-celom-zivotu-mozda-vise-necu-imati/158361|access-date=7 September 2017|work=mozzartsport.com|date=4 February 2017|language=sr|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170907213426/http://www.mozzartsport.com/vesti/cedi-osman-duda-ivkovic-velika-sreca-za-mene-kakvu-u-celom-zivotu-mozda-vise-necu-imati/158361|archive-date=7 September 2017|url-status=dead}} He has an older brother, [[Caner Osman|Caner]], who is also a basketball player.{{cite web | url=http://www.gazetebilkent.com/2014/09/29/cedi-osman-nam-i-diger-jedi-knight/ | title=Cedi Osman Nam-ı Diğer "Jedi Knight" ! | publisher=gazetebilkent.com | date=29 September 2014 | access-date=26 June 2015 | author=Özcan, Dilay | language=tr | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191013044753/https://www.gazetebilkent.com/2014/09/29/cedi-osman-nam-i-diger-jedi-knight/ | archive-date=13 October 2019 | url-status=dead }} He took up basketball in 2001, playing for [https://m.sport.novi.ba/clanak/350126/od-kk-rin-preko-kk-bosna-do-finala-eurobasketa-turcin-je-sve-poceo-u-sarajevu-a-sada-zivi-snove KK RIN Family Sarajevo] coached by legendary [[Rusmir Halilović]], and [[KK Bosna Royal|KK Bosna]]'s youth teams while attending elementary school in [[Sarajevo]].{{Cite web |title=NBA zvijezda Cedi Osman i poznata turska glumica borave u Sarajevu: Vratio sam se tamo gdje je sve počelo |url=https://www.klix.ba/magazin/showbiz/nba-zvijezda-cedi-osman-i-poznata-turska-glumica-borave-u-sarajevu-vratio-sam-se-tamo-gdje-je-sve-pocelo/230718019 |access-date=2025-09-12 |website=Klix.ba |language=hr}} Due to his paternal Turkish background, he became a Turkish citizen, as per Turkey's [[Right of return|right-of-return laws]]. Since then, he has also represented the [[Turkey men's national basketball team]]. ==Professional career== ===Anadolu Efes (2011–2017)=== [[File:Cedi Osman.JPG|left|thumb|Osman with Efes in 2014]] In 2007, Osman signed a youth team contract with [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] after his outstanding performance at KK Bosna. He played for the junior, star, and youth teams of Anadolu Efes. He was [[loan (sports)|loaned]] for the 2011–12 season to the Pertevniyal of the [[Turkish Basketball First League]], which was at the time the [[farm team]] of Anadolu Efes. In the summer of 2012, Osman signed a professional contract with the Anadolu Efes senior team. ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2017–2023)=== [[File:Cedi Osman 21 (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Osman shoots over [[David Nwaba]] during a game in 2021]] On 25 June 2015, Osman was selected with the 31st overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]], by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. His draft rights, along with those of [[Rakeem Christmas]] and a future draft pick, were then traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], in exchange for the draft rights to [[Tyus Jones]] that same night.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/draft-picks-150625|title=Cavaliers Acquire Draft Rights to Cedi Osman and Rakeem Christmas from Minnesota|date=25 June 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=26 June 2015}} On 18 July 2017, Osman signed with the Cleveland Cavaliers.{{cite news|title=Cavaliers Sign Cedi Osman|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/osman-signing-2017|access-date=18 July 2017|work=NBA|date=18 July 2017}} On 9 February 2018, Osman played 38 minutes in a 123-107 Cavaliers victory over the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. He contributed 16 points on 6-of-9 shooting while notching 6 rebounds, 5 assists, and 3 steals. The Cavaliers made it to the [[2018 NBA Finals]], but lost 4–0 to the [[Golden State Warriors]]. On 25 January 2019, in a 100–94 loss to the [[Miami Heat]], Osman scored a career-high 29 points. Four days later, Osman was named a participant for the 2019 [[Rising Stars Challenge]] as a member of the World Team.{{cite web |title=Doncic, Simmons headline Mtn Dew Ice Rising Stars rosters |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2019-mtn-dew-ice-rising-stars-roster-official-release |website=NBA.com |access-date=22 April 2021 |date=29 January 2019}} On 26 October 2019 Osman signed a contract extension with the Cavaliers.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/cedi-osman-extension-191026|title=Cavaliers and Cedi Osman Sign Multi-Year Contract Extension|date=26 October 2019|work=NBA.com|access-date=31 October 2021}} On 22 March 2022 Osman recorded his 500th 3 pointer as a member of the Cavaliers. This made him just the 9th Cavaliers player ever to join the 500+ 3 point club.{{Cite news|url=https://www.cleveland.com/cavs/2023/02/darius-garland-becomes-fastest-cavs-player-to-reach-500-career-3-pointers-behind-the-numbers.html|title=Darius Garland becomes fastest Cavs player to reach 500 career 3-pointers: Behind the Numbers|date=February 6, 2023|access-date=January 12, 2025|work=[[Cleveland.com]]|last=Noga|first=Joe|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230330021114/https://www.cleveland.com/cavs/2023/02/darius-garland-becomes-fastest-cavs-player-to-reach-500-career-3-pointers-behind-the-numbers.html|archive-date=March 30, 2023|url-status=live|url-access=subscription}} ===San Antonio Spurs (2023–2024)=== On 6 July 2023 Osman was traded to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] as part of a three-team trade with the [[Miami Heat]] and [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|title=SAN ANTONIO COMPLETES THREE-TEAM TRADE WITH CLEVELAND AND MIAMI|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/san-antonio-completes-three-team-trade-with-cleveland-and-miami|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2023|access-date=September 7, 2024}} ===Panathinaikos (2024–2026)=== [[File:Cedi Osman 6 Panathinaikos BC Euroleague 20251216 (9).jpg|left|thumb|Osman with [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] in 2025]] On 7 September 2024 Osman signed a one-year deal with the reigning [[EuroLeague]] and [[Greek Basketball League|Greek League]] champions [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]].{{cite web|title=Στον Παναθηναϊκό AKTOR o Τσεντί Οσμάν|url=https://www.paobc.gr/deltia-typoy/105661_ston-panathinaiko-aktor-o-tsenti-osman|website=PAOBC.gr|date=September 7, 2024|access-date=September 7, 2024|language=Greek}} On 9 April 2025, Osman agreed upon a two-year contract extension with the defending EuroLeague champions, worth 3.3 million euros. On April 15 of the same year, the deal was made official. On May 6, 2025, Osman was the deciding player in Panathinaikos' quarterfinal game 5 75-67 win over [[Anadolu Efes]], scoring 28 points, more than a third of his team's total tally, and collected 8 rebounds.{{cite web|title=Cedi Osman: 'When I heard them chant my name, I was emotional'|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/videos/cedi-osman-when-i-heard-them-chant-my-name-i-was-emotional/|date=May 7, 2025|access-date=May 9, 2025|language=English}}{{Dead link|date=February 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} On March 14, 2026, he was named the Most Valuable Player for Round 31 of the 2025-2026 EuroLeague Regular Season. He had 24 points, 5 rebounds, 3 assists, and 2 steals.{{cite web |title=Cedi Osman dominates Round 31 to claim EuroLeague MVP award |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1943565/cedi-osman-round-31-mvp-euroleague/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=30 March 2026 |language=en |date=14 March 2026}} ===PAOK (2026–present)=== On July 20, 2026, Osman signed a three–year deal with [[PAOK BC|PAOK Thessaloniki]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]] (GBL).{{Cite web|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/eurocup/news/paok-pulls-off-prized-pickup-of-cedi-osman/|title=PAOK pulls off prized pickup of Cedi Osman|date=July 20, 2026|website=euroleaguebasketball.net|access-date=July 20, 2026}} ==National team career== ===Junior national team=== Osman was a member of the junior national teams of Turkey. He played at the following tournaments with Turkey's junior national teams: the [[2011 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]], the [[2012 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]], the 2012 [[Albert Schweitzer Tournament]], where he won a bronze medal and was named the Most Talented Player, the [[2013 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]], where he won a gold medal, and at the [[2014 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]], where he also won a gold medal, and was named to the All-Tournament Team and selected as the [[Most valuable player|MVP]]. ===Senior national team=== After playing with the junior national teams of Turkey, Osman became a member of the senior men's [[Turkey national basketball team|Turkish national basketball team]]. With Turkey's senior national team, he has played at the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]], [[EuroBasket 2015]], [[2016 FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament – Manila|2016 Manila FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament]], [[EuroBasket 2017]], [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup]], [[EuroBasket 2022]], and [[EuroBasket 2025]].[https://web.archive.org/web/20161111123019/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/rpp//q/Cedi%20OSMAN/pid/93736/_//players.html Cedi OSMAN (TUR).]{{cite web |title=Cedi Osman |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/players/190655-cedi-osman |website=FIBA |access-date=September 16, 2025}} Lastly, he was the captain of the Turkish National Team in the EuroBasket 2025 and was one of the noteworthy players of the tournament. Cedi Osman made 29 successful three-points shots and became the tournament's top three-point shooter, was also selected for the "All-Star Second" team.{{cite web |title=All-Star Second Team |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/news/all-star-second-team-loyd-osman-avdija-markkanen-jokic |website=FIBA |access-date=September 16, 2025}} He finished the tournament with an average of 16 points per game. While playing the entire of the final game against [[Germany men's national basketball team|Germany]], he scored 23 points, but couldn't prevent the loss Turkey.{{cite web |title=Türkiye vs. Germany
